54:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Qamar In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty informs us about the approach of the Hour and the emptiness and passing of this world, as He the Almighty says: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it. And He also says: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. Hadiths have been narrated to that effect. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Amr ibn Ali told us: Khalaf ibn Musa told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) addressed his companions one day, and the sun was about to set, and only a small amount remained of it. He said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, nothing remains of this world compared to what has passed of it, except what remains of this day of yours compared to what has passed of it. We do not see of the sun except a little.” I say: This hadith is narrated by Khalaf ibn Musa ibn Khalaf al-Ami, on the authority of his father. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy ones, and he said: Perhaps he made a mistake. Another hadith that supports and explains the previous one Imam Ahmad said: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told us, Sharik told us, Salamah ibn Kuhayl told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the sun was at a high altitude after the afternoon prayer, and he said: Your lives are not compared to the lives of those who have passed except as what remains of the day in what has passed. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Mutraf told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I and the Hour were sent like this, and he pointed with his index and middle fingers. They both included it from the hadith of Abu Hazim, Salamah ibn Dinar. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Wahb Al-Suwai’i, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I and the Hour were sent like this to this, it almost overtook it. Al-A’mash brought his index and middle fingers together. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Ismail ibn Ubaydullah told me: Anas ibn Malik came to Al-Walid ibn Abdul-Malik and asked him: What did you hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) mention of the Hour? He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: You and the Hour are like these two. This was narrated only by Ahmad may God have mercy on him. This is also supported in the Sahih in the names of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), that he is the Gatherer who will gather the people on his feet. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz bin Asad told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, Hamid bin Hilal told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Umair, who said: Utbah bin Ghazwan delivered a sermon. Buhaiz said: He said before this time: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us. He praised God and thanked Him, then said: “As for what follows, the world has given notice of its end and has turned away, and nothing remains of it except a little bit of it, like the pouring of a vessel that its owner pours out. You will move from it to a home that will never end, so move from it with the best of what is in your presence, for it has been mentioned to us that a stone is thrown from the edge of Hell and falls into it for seventy years without reaching its bottom. By God, you will fill it. Are you amazed? By God, it has been mentioned to us that the distance between the gates of Paradise is a journey of forty years, and a day will come upon it when it will be full of people.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith, which was narrated only by Muslim. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub narrated to us, Ibn `Ulayyah narrated to me, `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib narrated to us, on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: We stopped in al-Mada`in and were a farsakh away from it. Then Friday came, and my father was present and I was present with him, and Hudhayfah delivered a sermon, saying: Verily, God says: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. Verily, the Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. Verily, the world has heralded a parting. Verily, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. So I said to my father: Will people race tomorrow? He said: O my son, you are ignorant. Racing is only in deeds. Then another Friday came, and we were present, and Hudhayfah delivered a sermon, saying: Verily, God the Almighty says: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. Verily, the world has heralded a parting. Verily, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. Verily, the destination is the Fire, and the one who races to Paradise is he who races first.” God the Almighty said: And the moon was split This happened during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), as mentioned in the numerous hadiths with authentic chains of transmission. It is proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Five have passed away: the Romans, the Smoke, the Lizam, the Batshah, and the moon." Muslim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Abd al-Wahhab told me, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon split into two halves until they saw Hira’ between them. And they both narrated it on the authority of Yunus bin Muhammad al-Mu’addib, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Qatada. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Yahya al-Qattan, and others, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, with this chain of transmission. Narrated by Jubair bin Mut’im (may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Kathir narrated to us, Sulayman bin Kathir narrated to us, on the authority of Hisayn bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and became two parts: one part on this mountain and one part on this mountain. They said: Muhammad has bewitched us. They said: If he has bewitched us, then he cannot bewitch all of the people. Imam Ahmad is the only one who narrated it from this source, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Dala’il on the authority of Muhammad bin Kathir, on the authority of his brother Sulayman bin Kathir, on the authority of Hisayn bin Abd al-Rahman. Thus, Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fadil and others on the authority of Hisayn, and Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman and Hisham, both of them on the authority of Hisayn on the authority of Jubayr ibn Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, and he mentioned it. Narrated by Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir told us, Bakr told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Arak bin Malik, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The moon split during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Bakr bin Mudar, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Arak, with a similar chain of narration. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: “The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’” He said: That has already happened. It was before the Hijra, when the moon split until they saw its two halves. Al-Awfi narrated something similar to this on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Amr al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qat’i told us, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The moon was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said, ‘The moon is magic.’ So the verse: “The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’” Narrated by Abdullah bin Omar Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz and Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Qadi told us: Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Abbas bin Muhammad Al-Duri told us: Wahb bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, regarding the words of God Almighty: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. He said: That happened during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It split into two halves, one from the side of the mountain and one from behind the mountain. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bear witness. Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in this way, through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Muslim said: It is similar to the narration of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. Narrated by Abdullah bin Masoud Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The moon split into two halves during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they could look at it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness. And this is how Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan bin Uyaynah with it. They also included it from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar Abdullah bin Sakhbarah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud with it. Ibn Jarir said: Isa bin Uthman bin Isa al-Ramli told us, my uncle Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina, and the moon split. A group took shelter behind the mountain, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness, bear witness. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Dhaha said, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah in Mecca. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Abu Uwanah told us, on the authority of al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh said: This is the magic of Ibn Abi Kabsha. He said: They said: Look at what the travelers bring you, for Muhammad cannot bewitch all of the people. He said: So the travelers came and said that. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri informed us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman informed us, Hisham informed us, Mughira informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The moon split in Mecca until it was in two parts. The infidels of Quraysh said to the people of Mecca: This is magic with which Ibn Abi Kabshah has bewitched you. Look at the travelers. If they saw what you saw, then he has spoken the truth, but if they did not see anything like what you saw, then it is magic with which he bewitched you. He said: The travelers were asked, and they came from every direction and said: We saw it. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Mughira with it, and he added: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim informed me, Ibn Ulayyah informed us, Ayyub informed us, on the authority of Muhammad, who is Ibn Sirin, who said: I was told that Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, used to say: The moon has split. Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad bin Amara told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I saw the mountain from the opening of the moon when it split. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Muammil, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until I saw the mountain from between the two openings of the moon. Layth said, on the authority of Mujahid: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it became two parts, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: Bear witness, O Abu Bakr. The polytheists said: The moon was bewitched until it split. And the Almighty said, And if they see a sign, meaning a proof, argument, or evidence, they turn away, meaning they do not submit to it, but rather they turn away from it and leave it behind them. And they say, ‘Persistent magic,’ meaning they say, This is magic that has bewitched us. The meaning of persistent is going away, as Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: It is false and disappearing and has no permanence. “And they denied and followed their desires,” meaning they denied the truth when it came to them, and they followed what their opinions and desires commanded them to do due to their ignorance and foolishness of mind. His statement, And every matter is settled. Qatada said: Its meaning is that good will happen to the people of good, and evil will happen to the people of evil. Ibn Jurayj said: It is settled with its people. Mujahid said: And every matter is settled, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi said: It is settled, meaning it will happen. God the Almighty says: And there has certainly come to them from the report, meaning from the report of the nations who denied the messengers and the punishment, humiliation, and torment that befell them, as is recited to them in the Quran. In which there is a deterrent, meaning in which there is an admonition to them against polytheism and persisting in their denial. God the Almighty says: A perfect wisdom, meaning in His guidance of whomever He guides and His misguidance of whomever He misguides. So of what use are warnings? Meaning, what use are warnings for someone for whom God has decreed misery and sealed his heart? Who can guide him after God? This verse is similar to His statement, "Say, 'To God belongs the perfect argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.'" And His statement, And neither signs nor warners avail a people who do not believe.

54:9: God the Almighty says: Your people denied before you, O Muhammad. The people of Noah denied Our servant meaning they openly denied him and accused him of madness. And they said, 'He is mad,' but he was warned. Mujahid said: And he was warned. That is, he became insane. It was also said: And he was warned means they rebuked him, admonished him, and threatened him, If you do not desist, O Noah, you will be among those who are stoned. Ibn Zayd said this, and this is a good interpretation. So he called upon his Lord, 'Indeed, I am overcome, so aid' meaning I am weak against these people and against resisting them, so aid your religion. God the Almighty said: Then We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water. Al-Suddi said: This is a lot. And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth meaning all parts of the earth gushed forth, even the ovens, which are the places of fire, gushed forth springs. And the waters met meaning from the sky and the earth by a matter already decreed. That is, a matter already decreed. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water. Plenty of rain had not come from the sky before or after that day except from clouds. The gates of heaven were opened with water that day without clouds, so the two waters met according to a predestined matter. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Ali about the sky and he said: It is the opening of the sky, and from it the sky was opened with pouring water. And We carried him on planks and nails. Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Qurazi, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: They are nails, and Ibn Jarir chose this. He said: Its singular is dasar. It is also said dasir, just as it is said habayk and habak, and the plural is habak. Mujahid said: Dasr is the ribs of the ship. Ikrimah and al-Hasan said: It is its front with which the waves strike. Ad-Dahhak said: Its two ends and its base. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is its kallak, meaning its front. 54:33: God Almighty says, informing us about the people of Lot, how they denied their Messenger and disobeyed him, and committed the abhorrent act of having intercourse with males, which is an indecency that no one in the world had ever committed before them. For this reason, God destroyed them in a way that no other nation had ever destroyed. God Almighty commanded Gabriel, peace be upon him, to carry their cities until they reached the heavens, then turned them upside down upon them and sent them down, followed by stones of layered baked clay. For this reason, He said here: Indeed, We sent upon them a hailstone, which are the stones, “except the family of Lot. We saved them at dawn,” meaning they came out at the end of the night and were saved from what had befallen their people. Not one man from Lot’s people believed in him, not even his wife, who was afflicted with what had befallen her people. God’s Prophet Lot and his daughters emerged from among them unharmed, no harm had touched them. For this reason, God Almighty said: “Thus do We reward the grateful. And He had warned them of Our punishment,” meaning, before the punishment came upon them, they had He warned them of the punishment and torment of God, but they did not pay attention to it or listen to it. Rather, they doubted it and disputed about it. And they had indeed tried to seduce him from his guest That was on the night when the angels Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil came to him in the guise of handsome young men, as a trial from God upon them. So Lot, peace be upon him, hosted them. His wicked old wife sent word to her people about Lot's guests, so they came running to him from every direction. Lot closed the door behind them, so they tried to break it down. That was in the evening, and Lot, peace be upon him, was defending them and preventing them from protecting his guests, saying to them: These are my daughters meaning their wives if you should do something. "They said: You know that we have no right to your daughters meaning we have no interest in them and indeed, you know what we want." When the situation became intense and they refused to do anything but enter, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came out to them and struck their eyes with the tip of his wing, so their eyes were blinded. It is said that they sank from their faces, and it is said that they had no eyes left at all, so they turned back, feeling themselves against the walls, and threatening Lot, peace be upon him, until morning. God Almighty said: And indeed, early in the morning, a lasting punishment overtook them. That is, there is no way for them to escape from it or escape it. “So taste My punishment and warning. And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?”

Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Rib’i on the authority of Ali, with this chain of transmission. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wahb and others, on the authority of Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God wrote the destinies of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Ibn Wahb added, and His Throne was over the water. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: It is good, authentic, and rare. And the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. This is a statement about the influence of His will on His creation, just as He informed us about the influence of His decree on them, saying: And Our command is but one. That is, We only command something once, and do not need to confirm it with a second. Thus, what We command is achieved and present, like the twinkling of an eye, not delayed for the blink of an eye. How beautiful is what some poets said: If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. And the Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly destroyed your followers meaning your likes and predecessors from the previous nations who denied the Messengers. So is there any who will remember? meaning is there anyone who will take heed of what God has humiliated those people with and decreed for them of punishment, as the Almighty said: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as He did with their followers before. And the Almighty’s saying: And everything they did is in the scriptures meaning it is written down for them in the books in the hands of the angels, peace be upon them. And every small and great meaning of their deeds is recorded meaning it is collected for them and recorded in their scrolls, leaving out nothing small or great without enumerating it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir told us, Saeed bin Muslim bin Bank told us, I heard Amir bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, Aouf bin Al-Harith, who was Aisha’s maternal nephew, told me, on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: O Aisha, beware of small sins, for God will seek them out. Narrated by An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah on the authority of Saeed bin Muslim bin Bank Al-Madani. Ahmad, Ibn Ma’in, Abu Hatim and others authenticated him. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Saeed bin Muslim from another chain of transmission. Then Saeed said: I narrated this hadith to Amir bin Hisham, and he said to me: Woe to you, O Saeed bin Muslim! Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told me that he committed a sin and considered it small, so someone came to him in his sleep and said: O Sulayman: Do not underestimate small sins, for tomorrow the small will become big again. Even if the young one has lived long before God, he is recorded in a long line. Resist your passion for unemployment, do not be difficult to control and roll up your sleeves When a lover loves his God, his heart soars and his mind is inspired. So ask God for your guidance, my daughter, for your Lord is sufficient as a guide and a supporter. God the Almighty says: In a seat of truth, meaning in the abode of God’s honor, pleasure, favor, grace, generosity, and kindness. Near a Sovereign, All-Powerful, meaning near the Great King, the Creator of all things and their Determiner. He is All-Powerful over whatever they ask for and desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Amr ibn Aws, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, narrating it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “The just will be with God on pulpits of light, at the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both of His hands are right. 54:55: The Almighty tells us about the criminals that they are in error from the truth and are in a state of doubt and confusion in their opinions, and this includes everyone who is described as such from disbelievers and innovators from all sects. Then the Almighty said: The Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces, meaning just as they were in a state of doubt and hesitation that caused them to be inherited from the Fire, and just as they were in error, they will be dragged into it on their faces, not knowing where they are going, and it will be said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke: Taste the touch of Hellfire. And the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, all things We created with predestination is like His saying: And He created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination and His saying the Almighty: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned, Who determined and guided meaning He determined a predestination and guided the creatures to it. For this reason, the Imams of the Sunnah use this noble verse as evidence to prove God’s predestination prior to His creation, which is His knowledge of things before they come into being and His writing of them before they come into being. They responded with this verse and similar verses and the authentic hadiths that have been reported in their meaning to the Qadarites, who emerged at the end of the era of the Companions. We have discussed this matter in detail and the hadiths that have been reported regarding it in the commentary on the Book of Faith in Sahih al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him. We will mention here the hadiths related to this noble verse. Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Isma`il as-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ibad ibn Ja`far, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to argue with him about predestination, so the verse, “The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: ‘Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, We have created all things with predestination.’” was revealed. Muslim, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it in this way from the hadith of Waki`, on the authority of Sufyan ath-Thawri. Al-Bazzar said: `Amr ibn `Ali narrated to us, ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith narrated to us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: These verses, “Indeed, the criminals are in error and Blaze. The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: ‘Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, We have created all things with predestination.’” were not revealed except about the people of predestination. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sahl bin Salih al-Antaki told us, Qara bin Habib told me, on the authority of Kinanah, Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Sa`id bin `Amr bin Ja`dah, on the authority of Ibn Zararah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited this verse: “Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, all things We created with predestination.” He said: It was revealed concerning people from my nation who will be at the end of time and will deny God’s predestination. Al-Hasan bin Arafa narrated to us: Marwan bin Shuja’ al-Jazari narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, who said: I came to Ibn Abbas while he was drawing water from Zamzam, and the lower parts of his clothes were wet. I said to him, He has spoken about predestination. He said, Have they really done that? I said, Yes. He said, “By God, this verse was only revealed about them: ‘Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, We have created all things with predestination.’” They are the worst of this nation, so do not visit their sick or pray over their dead. If I see one of them, I will put out his eyes with these two fingers.” Imam Ahmad narrated it from another chain of transmission, and it includes a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), in which he said: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, al-Awza’i narrated to us, on the authority of some of his brothers, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ubayd al-Makki, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: It was said to him, A man has come to us who lies about predestination. He said, Guide me to him, even though he is blind. They said, What will you do with him, O Abu Abbas? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I get hold of him, I will bite his nose until I cut it off, and if his neck falls into my hands, I will crush it, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “It is as if I see the women of Banu Fihr going around the Khazraj, their buttocks clasping, as polytheists. This is the beginning of the polytheism of this nation. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, their evil opinion will end until they prevent God from having decreed good, just as they prevented Him from having decreed evil.” Then Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Mughira on the authority of al-Awza’i on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Hajjaj on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubayd, and he mentioned something similar, but they did not narrate it. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told us: Abu Sakhr told me on the authority of Nafi’ who said: Ibn Umar had a friend from the people of Ash-Sham who used to write to him. Abdullah bin Umar wrote to him, saying, “I have heard that you have spoken about predestination, so beware of writing to me, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘There will be people in my nation who will deny predestination.’” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Hanbal. Ahmad said: Anas ibn Ayyad narrated to us, Umar ibn Abdullah, the freed slave of Ghafra, narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every nation has its Magians, and the Magians of my nation are those who say there is no predestination. If they fall ill, do not visit them, and if they die, do not attend their funeral.” None of the authors of the Six Books narrated it from this chain of narration. Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rashdin narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr Hamid ibn Ziyad, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There will be transformations in this nation, and that will be among those who deny predestination and the heretics. At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abu Sakhr Hamid ibn Ziyad with this chain of narration. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih gharib. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn At-Tabba’ narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Ziyad ibn Sa’d, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus Al-Yamani, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything is predestiny, even laziness and intelligence. Muslim narrated it alone from the hadith of Malik. In the authentic hadith: “Seek help from God and do not lose hope. If something befalls you, say: God has decreed it and whatever He wills He does. Do not say: ‘If only I had done such and such, then such and such would have happened,’ for ‘if’ opens the door to the work of Satan.” In the hadith of Ibn Abbas, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: “Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with something that God had not decreed for you, they would not benefit you. And if they were to gather together to harm you with something that God had not decreed for you, they would not harm you. The pens have dried and the pages have been folded.” Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan ibn Suwar told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Ziyad, Ubadah ibn Al-Walid ibn Ubadah told me, my father told me: I entered upon Ubadah while he was sick and I was imagining death. I said: O my father, advise me and strive hard for me. He said: Sit me up. When they sat him up, he said: O my son, you have not tasted faith and you have not attained the true right of knowledge of God until you believe in destiny, both its good and its evil. I said: O my father, how can I know what is the good and evil of destiny?” He said: Know that what missed you was not going to befall you, and what befell you was not going to miss you. My son, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He said to it, ‘Write.’ And it wrote down in that instant what would happen until the Day of Resurrection.” My son, if you die not believing this, you will enter Hell. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Yahya bin Musa Al-Balkhi on the authority of Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi on the authority of Abdul-Wahid bin Saleem on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah on the authority of Al-Walid bin Ubadah on the authority of his father, with this chain of transmission. He said: It is hasan saheeh ghareeb. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Rib’i bin Kharash, on the authority of a man on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “No one truly believes until he believes in four things: he bears witness that there is no god but God, and that I am the Messenger of God who has been sent with the truth, he believes in resurrection after death, and he believes in divine destiny, both its good and its bad.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise on the authority of An-Nadr bin Shumayl on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Rib’i on the authority of Ali, and he mentioned it and said: This is more authentic in my opinion. Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Rib’i on the authority of Ali, with this chain of transmission. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wahb and others, on the authority of Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God wrote the destinies of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Ibn Wahb added, and His Throne was over the water. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: It is good, authentic, and rare. And the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. This is a statement about the influence of His will on His creation, just as He informed us about the influence of His decree on them, saying: And Our command is but one. That is, We only command something once, and do not need to confirm it with a second. Thus, what We command is achieved and present, like the twinkling of an eye, not delayed for the blink of an eye. How beautiful is what some poets said: If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. And the Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly destroyed your followers meaning your likes and predecessors from the previous nations who denied the Messengers. So is there any who will remember? meaning is there anyone who will take heed of what God has humiliated those people with and decreed for them of punishment, as the Almighty said: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as He did with their followers before. And the Almighty’s saying: And everything they did is in the scriptures meaning it is written down for them in the books in the hands of the angels, peace be upon them. And every small and great meaning of their deeds is recorded meaning it is collected for them and recorded in their scrolls, leaving out nothing small or great without enumerating it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir told us, Saeed bin Muslim bin Bank told us, I heard Amir bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, Aouf bin Al-Harith, who was Aisha’s maternal nephew, told me, on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: O Aisha, beware of small sins, for God will seek them out. Narrated by An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah on the authority of Saeed bin Muslim bin Bank Al-Madani. Ahmad, Ibn Ma’in, Abu Hatim and others authenticated him. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Saeed bin Muslim from another chain of transmission. Then Saeed said: I narrated this hadith to Amir bin Hisham, and he said to me: Woe to you, O Saeed bin Muslim! Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told me that he committed a sin and considered it small, so someone came to him in his sleep and said: O Sulayman: Do not underestimate small sins, for tomorrow the small will become big again. Even if the young one has lived long before God, he is recorded in a long line. Resist your passion for unemployment, do not be difficult to control and roll up your sleeves When a lover loves his God, his heart soars and his mind is inspired. So ask God for your guidance, my daughter, for your Lord is sufficient as a guide and a supporter. God the Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers, meaning the opposite of what the wretched will be in of misguidance, burning, and being dragged into the Fire on their faces, along with rebuke, reprimand, and threats. God the Almighty says: In a seat of truth, meaning in the abode of God’s honor, pleasure, favor, grace, generosity, and kindness. Near a Sovereign, All-Powerful, meaning near the Great King, the Creator of all things and their Determiner. He is All-Powerful over whatever they ask for and desire. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Amr ibn Aws, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, narrating it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “The just will be with God on pulpits of light, at the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both of His hands are right. Those who are just in their judgment, their families, and those under their authority.” Muslim and An-Nasa’i alone transmitted it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with a similar chain of transmission. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Aqrabat. Praise and thanks be to God, and with Him is success and protection.
